about.title: Piedmont Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Piedmont is a small city, and in 2025 its public collision record showed 12 injury crashes, 13 people hurt, and no traffic deaths within city limits. It does not tell the whole story for Piedmont families, though. Wrongful death claims arise from far more than car crashes: a fall on poorly maintained property, an error in medical care, a workplace accident, or a collision that happened while a Piedmont resident was driving elsewhere in Alameda County. When a death like that occurs, California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring a civil claim first, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when there is no one in that first group. The claim is separate from any criminal case and generally must be filed within two years of the death, sooner if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Piedmont families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so your energy can stay with the people who need you.

whyChoose.title: Why Piedmont Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clear answers about who can file
items.desc: California gives the first right to bring a wrongful death claim to the spouse or domestic partner and children, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other circumstances. An attorney can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is watched from day one
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting connected early keeps those dates from slipping by during a hard season.

items.title: Losses that go beyond the bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs and the financial support your relative would have provided, but also the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Piedmont recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Can my family still bring a claim if my relative died in a crash nearby?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim depends on how and where the death happened, not on where the family lives. Piedmont's own collision record centers on corridors like Grand Avenue, Oakland Avenue, Highland Avenue, and the 100 block of Hampton Road, but many residents drive, bike, and walk well beyond city limits every day. An attorney can review a crash anywhere in Alameda County or the wider Bay Area.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same thing as the criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are two separate proceedings. A criminal case is brought by the district attorney and focuses on punishment; a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family to recover their losses. The civil claim can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed, and the outcome of one does not decide the other.

items.question: How long do we have to file in California, and does it matter who caused the death?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death. If the responsible party is a government entity, such as a city or a public transit agency, a formal claim usually must be presented in a much shorter period before any lawsuit can be filed. Because the identity of the responsible party changes the timeline, it helps to speak with an attorney soon rather than waiting for things to settle down.
